errors.english: Thus concludes the Avadāna of Śrīsenā
errors.why: The hero of Kalpalatā 2 is King Śrīsena (dPal gyi sde), masculine; 'Śrīsenā' with long final ā misnames him (the ā in śrīsenāvadāna is sandhi).

note: Colophon and opening verses of the Śrīsena/third chapter are faithfully rendered; the colophon verse is translated twice (once as the Sanskrit, once as the Tibetan), which is redundant but not wrong.

errors.english: transforming the mental continuum [note: original: "rgyud," referring to the stream of consciousness]
errors.why: The continuum transformed by the application (prayoga) is the series of the mantra itself (producing successive distinctions in what has arisen), not the practitioner's stream of consciousness.

note: The anti-Mīmāṃsā argument on mantra efficacy and the Brahmin/śūdra point is followed correctly; one misleading gloss on rgyud.

errors.english: The cause is the habituated tendencies (vasana) karmic imprints or latencies that correspond to the equality or inequality of bodies.
errors.why: The Tibetan says that, whether bodies are alike or unlike, the cause is the latent impressions of a corresponding (homogeneous) habituation; the English makes the impressions track the bodies' likeness, undoing the argument that consciousness does not follow the body.

note: The anti-materialist argument (milk analogy, regress, bag chags as cause) is mostly well rendered.

errors.english: offer up considerable non-benefit, accumulating unique blame known to the wise
errors.why: The Tibetan describes the king accumulating uncommon (unshared) misdeeds that are 'adept at bestowing no small harm'; 'known to the wise' misparses mkhas pa, which here means 'skilled at' and qualifies the misdeeds.

note: Candrakīrti's buffalo-sacrifice and butcher's-son illustrations and the two root verses are rendered accurately.
Accurate rendering of the Vinaya discussion of when an act counts as done (jñaptidvitīya/caturtha) and the boundary-establishing case to Upāli.

errors.english: made them take up residence with him
errors.why: gnas 'char ba is the Vinaya term for taking dependence (niśraya) on a preceptor/teacher; Udāyin made them take niśraya under him, not merely reside with him.

errors.english: Except to ensure that these do not produce impurities, other things should be cast away.
errors.why: The clause continues 'srog chags [dag] mi skye ba' from the previous side (except where living creatures do not breed, the rest is to be discarded); 'impurities' is not in the text.

note: Good rendering of the end of the bedding pāyattika and the opening nidāna of the expulsion rule with Udāyin (Char ka).
The apoha discussion (deceptive non-exclusion word-meaning, isolated words like 'prameya', helping the listener) is closely and correctly followed.

errors.why: The sentence closes the preceding verses ('…' — these are the summary verses); the English turns it into a heading introducing the following prose, which is commentary, not verse.

fix.replace: The above are the summary verses.

errors.english: then the words of those with different philosophical views would not engage with objects without a cause
errors.why: The verse says words would not apply, being causeless, to the objects (posited) by other philosophical views; 'other views' qualifies the objects, and 'causeless' qualifies the words' application, not the objects.

errors.english: a substantial cause of the nature one desires
errors.why: ji ltar 'dod pa here means 'as (the opponent) asserts it': the probandum is that the object lacks a material cause of the nature that is claimed, not one that is desired.

note: The apoha/pradhāna argument is broadly followed, but the summary-verse marker is misplaced and a key verse is misconstrued.

errors.why: This is a Mūlasarvāstivāda text; the Sanskrit term is saṃghāvaśeṣa (the Pali form sanghadisesa is also used again for the fourth mode).

errors.english: He must be mindful and remain very composed.
errors.why: The duties concern the text: he must commit the sūtra to memory and make it thoroughly fluent/settled, not be mindful and personally composed.

note: The five modes of prātimokṣa recitation and the duties of reciter, elder and middle monk are correctly rendered apart from a Pali term and one misread duty.

errors.english: is a plural term used to express clarity
errors.why: gsal ba here is vyakti, the individual instances: the plural is used because the individuals are meant, not 'to express clarity'.

fix.find: is a plural term used to express clarity
fix.replace: is a plural, used because the individual instances (vyakti) are meant

errors.english: If a support makes the state of destruction occur through itself or another
errors.why: The Tibetan says 'if the support causes the perishing thing to endure (gnas byed)', i.e. maintains it, not that it brings about destruction.

errors.english: that which abides in an object does not actually meet with the object
errors.why: Two things are denied ultimately: there is no residing in the object, nor any contact with the object; the English makes the first the subject of the second.
mtshams sbyor ba is pratisandhi, rebirth-linking: the mental consciousness that links rebirth is what is called 'sattva'.

errors.english: the fuel (upādāna) appropriation/material cause and that which arises from the fuel—the light and the lamp
errors.why: The material cause and its product are the lamp(flame) and the light; there is no fuel here, and 'arises from the fuel' misidentifies the relata of the support-supported relation.

note: The refutation of a support (āśraya) for the mind is followed in outline, but several technical terms (vyakti, pratisandhi, upādāna) and one key clause are misread.
